question.text: The value of a new sewing machine is $\$640.$ If the machine's value depreciates by one half every year, what will be its value after three years?
question.explanation:
The initial value is $640$ dollars, and its value reduces by $\dfrac 1 2$ every year.

Therefore:

  • After $1$ year, the value will be $640 \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ dollars.

  • After ${\color{blue}{2}}$ years, the value will be $640 \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\color{blue}{2}}$ dollars.

  • After ${\color{blue}{3}}$ years, the value will be $640 \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\color{blue}{3}}$ dollars.

Evaluating the last expression, we get

\[ 640 \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3=80. \]

Therefore, the sewing machine will be worth $\$80$ after $3$ years.

example.title: Creating an Exponential Decay Expression From a Decay Factor

question.text: A car is purchased for $\$18\,000$ and its value depreciates (decreases) by $\dfrac{1}{5}$ per year. What will be the value of the car in $8$ years?
question.explanation:
If the value reduces by $\dfrac 1 5,$ it means that $\dfrac 4 5$ of its value remains every year.

Therefore:

  • After $1$ year, the value of the car will be $\$18\,000\cdot \left(\dfrac 4 5\right).$

  • After $\color{blue}2$ years, the value of the car will be $\$18\,000\cdot \left(\dfrac 4 5\right)^{\color{blue}2}.$

  • After $\color{blue}3$ years, the value of the car will be $\$18\,000\cdot \left(\dfrac 4 5\right)^{\color{blue}3}.$

  • $\ldots$

Repeating this pattern, we see that the value of the car will be $\$18\,000\cdot \left(\dfrac 4 5\right)^{\color{blue}8}$ in $\color{blue}8$ years.

example.title: Creating an Exponential Decay Expression From a Decay Factor

question.text: Initially, a company had $1\,200$ subscribers for its online video channel. The number of subscribers then decreased at a rate of $4\%$ every year. Approximately how many subscribers remained after $7$ years?
question.explanation:
The number $4\%$ (expressed as a decimal) is equal to $0.04.$ Therefore, a decrease of $4\%$ corresponds to multiplication by a factor of:

\[ 1-0.04 = 0.96 \]

Therefore:

  • After $1$ year, there were $1\,200\cdot (0.96)$ subscribers.

  • After $2$ years, there were approximately $1\,200\cdot (0.96)^{\color{blue}2}$ subscribers.

  • After $3$ years, there were approximately $1\,200\cdot (0.96)^{\color{blue}3}$ subscribers.

  • $\ldots$

Repeating this pattern, we see that there were approximately $1\,200\cdot (0.96)^{\color{blue}7}$ subscribers after $7$ years.
